Autopsy.question: 1) The first medico-legal autopsy was performed by:
Autopsy.exp: The first medico-legal autopsy was performed by Bartolomeo da Varignana. It was done in Bologna, Italy, in 1302.

Autopsy.question: 2) The first medico-legal autopsy was performed in:
Autopsy.exp: The first medico-legal autopsy was performed at Bologna in Italy. The associated year was 1302.

Autopsy.question: 3) The year of first medico-legal autopsy was:
Autopsy.exp: Bartolomeo da Varignana performed the first medico-legal autopsy in 1302 at Bologna, Italy.

Autopsy.question: 4) Consent in medico-legal autopsy is:
Autopsy.exp: Medico-legal autopsy is performed under legal authority. Consent of relatives is not required in such cases.

Autopsy.question: 5) The main purpose of medico-legal autopsy is:
Autopsy.exp: Medico-legal or forensic autopsy is done for legal investigation. It helps determine cause, manner and circumstances of death.

Autopsy.question: 6) Medico-legal autopsy is usually performed by:
Autopsy.exp: Medico-legal autopsy is performed by a forensic pathologist or an authorized doctor. It has legal importance.

Autopsy.question: 7) Clinical autopsy is mainly performed for:
Autopsy.exp: Clinical or pathological autopsy is done mainly for medical research and clinicopathological correlation. It requires consent.

Autopsy.question: 8) Clinical autopsy is usually performed by:
Autopsy.exp: Clinical autopsy is done by a hospital pathologist. Its purpose is medical, not legal investigation.

Autopsy.question: 9) Anatomical autopsy is mainly performed for:
Autopsy.exp: Anatomical or academic autopsy is done for teaching anatomy. It requires consent or body donation.

Autopsy.question: 10) Anatomical autopsy is usually handled by:
Autopsy.exp: Anatomical autopsy is performed by the anatomy department. It is primarily for teaching and academic purposes.

Autopsy.question: 11) Legal aspect is present in:
Autopsy.exp: Medico-legal autopsy has legal significance because it is done for investigation of death. Clinical and anatomical autopsies do not primarily serve legal purposes.

Autopsy.question: 12) Consent is required in:
Autopsy.exp: Clinical autopsy requires consent because it is not ordered for legal investigation. Medico-legal autopsy is done under legal authority.

Autopsy.question: 13) Consent for anatomical autopsy is commonly based on:
Autopsy.exp: Anatomical autopsy requires consent or donation of the body. It is performed for teaching anatomy.

Autopsy.question: 14) A complete autopsy with necessary tests where cause of death is not found is called:
Autopsy.exp: Negative autopsy means complete autopsy and investigations are done, but the cause of death remains undetermined.

Autopsy.question: 15) Cause of death exists but is hidden or difficult to detect in:
Autopsy.exp: In obscure autopsy, the cause of death exists but is difficult to identify. It may be missed unless carefully searched.

Autopsy.question: 16) Autopsy repeated after a disputed first autopsy is:
Autopsy.exp: Second autopsy is done when the first autopsy is questioned, incomplete, disputed or needs expert re-evaluation.

Autopsy.question: 17) A questioned or incomplete first autopsy report may require:
Autopsy.exp: Second autopsy helps re-evaluate findings when the first autopsy is doubtful, incomplete or disputed.

Autopsy.question: 18) The document requesting postmortem examination is:
Autopsy.exp: Chalan is the requisition or request for postmortem examination. It contains identity, case details and request for autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 19) Preliminary investigation into cause and circumstances of death is:
Autopsy.exp: Inquest is a preliminary investigation into the cause and circumstances of death. It records external findings and scene-related information.

Autopsy.question: 20) Chalan is usually prepared by:
Autopsy.exp: Chalan is prepared by the investigating police officer. It formally requests postmortem examination.

Autopsy.question: 21) Inquest is prepared by:
Autopsy.exp: Inquest is prepared by a police officer or magistrate acting as inquest officer. It documents preliminary facts before autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 22) External findings on the body are mainly recorded in:
Autopsy.exp: Inquest report includes external findings on the body, scene observations and witness statements. Chalan is mainly a requisition.

Autopsy.question: 23) Identity of deceased and request for autopsy are mainly included in:
Autopsy.exp: Chalan contains identity of the deceased, case details and request for postmortem examination.

Autopsy.question: 24) One important prerequisite before medico-legal autopsy is:
Autopsy.exp: Inquest report is required before medico-legal autopsy. It provides preliminary information regarding death and circumstances.

Autopsy.question: 25) Another important prerequisite before medico-legal autopsy is:
Autopsy.exp: Chalan is the official requisition for postmortem examination. Without proper chalan, autopsy should not proceed.

Autopsy.question: 26) Identification of the dead body before autopsy is done by:
Autopsy.exp: Identification by police personnel is required before medico-legal autopsy. It ensures that the correct body is examined.

Autopsy.question: 27) Autopsy must be conducted by:
Autopsy.exp: Medico-legal autopsy should be performed by an authorized doctor. The doctor must have legal authority to conduct it.

Autopsy.question: 28) A proper autopsy requires:
Autopsy.exp: An ideal morgue and proper light are prerequisites for autopsy. They help ensure proper examination and documentation.

Autopsy.question: 29) Professor or lecturer of Forensic Medicine in a government medical college is:
Autopsy.exp: Professor or lecturer of Forensic Medicine department of a government medical college is authorized to perform medico-legal autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 30) Civil Surgeon may act as:
Autopsy.exp: Civil Surgeon is one of the authorized doctors for medico-legal autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 31) Resident Medical Officer is included among:
Autopsy.exp: Resident Medical Officer is listed among the authorized doctors who may conduct medico-legal autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 32) Medico-legal autopsy is ordered by:
Autopsy.exp: Medico-legal autopsy is ordered by magistrate, police or other legal authority. It does not depend on family permission.

Autopsy.question: 33) Absence of chalan is a ground for:
Autopsy.exp: Absence or incomplete chalan is a valid reason to refuse autopsy. Chalan is the formal request for postmortem examination.

Autopsy.question: 34) Incomplete inquest report is a ground for:
Autopsy.exp: Absence or incomplete inquest report makes legal documentation inadequate. Autopsy may be refused until proper documents are provided.

Autopsy.question: 35) Body not identified by police is a ground for:
Autopsy.exp: Police identification is necessary before medico-legal autopsy. Without identification, the risk of wrong-body examination remains.

Autopsy.question: 36) Death from highly infectious disease such as rabies may lead to:
Autopsy.exp: Death from highly infectious diseases such as rabies may be a condition to refuse autopsy because of safety risk.

Autopsy.question: 37) Magistrate’s inquest is required in death:
Autopsy.exp: Death in police custody or during police interrogation requires magistrate’s inquest due to its legal sensitivity.

Autopsy.question: 38) Death due to police firing requires:
Autopsy.exp: Death due to police firing is a legally sensitive death. Magistrate’s inquest is required.

Autopsy.question: 39) Death in prison requires:
Autopsy.exp: Death in prison, reformatory or Borstal school requires magistrate’s inquest. Custodial deaths need special legal scrutiny.

Autopsy.question: 40) Death in psychiatric hospital requires:
Autopsy.exp: Death in psychiatric hospital is included among conditions requiring magistrate’s inquest.

Autopsy.question: 41) Dowry death requires:
Autopsy.exp: Dowry death requires magistrate’s inquest because it is a serious medico-legal death.

Autopsy.question: 42) Exhumation case requires:
Autopsy.exp: Exhumation cases require magistrate’s inquest. It involves legal digging out of a buried body.

Autopsy.question: 43) Death, disappearance or rape allegation while in custody requires:
Autopsy.exp: Custodial death, disappearance or rape allegation requires magistrate’s inquest because of high legal importance.

Autopsy.question: 44) The most common autopsy incision is:
Autopsy.exp: I-shaped incision is the most common autopsy incision. It is simple, fast and gives full access to thoracic and abdominal cavities.

Autopsy.question: 45) I-shaped incision extends from:
Autopsy.exp: I-shaped incision is a straight midline incision extending from chin to pubis. It is commonly used in autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 46) Y-shaped incision extends from:
Autopsy.option2: Each shoulder to xiphisternum and then to pubis
Autopsy.option3: Behind ears to sternum and then downwards
Autopsy.option4: Horizontal and vertical cuts on skull
Autopsy.exp: Y-shaped incision begins from each shoulder, meets at the xiphisternum and continues down to the pubis.

Autopsy.question: 47) Y-shaped incision allows better exposure of:
Autopsy.exp: Y-shaped incision provides better exposure of neck vessels and chest cavity. It is useful when upper thoracic and neck exposure is needed.

Autopsy.question: 48) Modified Y or U-shaped incision begins from:
Autopsy.exp: Modified Y/U-shaped incision curves from behind the ears to the sternum and then downwards.

Autopsy.question: 49) Modified Y/U-shaped incision is especially useful in:
Autopsy.exp: Modified Y/U-shaped incision gives better exposure of face and neck structures. It is useful in hanging, strangulation and neck trauma.

Autopsy.question: 50) The incision used for cranial cavity is:
Autopsy.exp: Cruciate or T-shaped incision is used for cranial cavity. It is the standard incision for brain removal.

Autopsy.question: 51) Standard incision for brain removal is:
Autopsy.exp: The cruciate or T-shaped incision is made on the skull for opening the cranial cavity and removing the brain.

Autopsy.question: 52) Simple and fast access to thoracic and abdominal cavity is provided by:
Autopsy.exp: I-shaped incision is simple and fast. It gives good access to thoracic and abdominal organs.

Autopsy.question: 53) Face and neck exposure is best provided by:
Autopsy.exp: Modified Y/U-shaped incision is designed for better exposure of face and neck. It is useful in suspected neck injuries.

Autopsy.question: 54) The best document pair before medico-legal autopsy is:
Autopsy.exp: Chalan requests the postmortem examination, and inquest report records preliminary findings and circumstances. Both are essential before medico-legal autopsy.

Autopsy.question: 55) Chalan is best described as:
Autopsy.option2: Final opinion on cause of death
Autopsy.exp: Chalan is the official request for postmortem examination. Inquest is the preliminary investigation into cause and circumstances of death.
